title: 5 Cold Can Hacks to Beat the Dhaka Heat
excerpt: No fridge space? No problem. Five quick tricks to get your cans ice-cold in minutes.
body:
When the Dhaka sun is at its fiercest, a lukewarm can is a small tragedy. The good news: you do not need a bigger fridge to fix it. Here are five tricks we swear by at Drink it HQ.

Here is how to get your cans ice-cold, fast:

  1. The salt-ice bath: Fill a bucket with ice and water, add a generous handful of salt and spin the cans for three minutes. Salt lowers the freezing point of the water, so the bath gets colder than plain ice.
  2. The wet paper towel: Wrap a can in a damp paper towel and place it in the freezer for 15 minutes. Set a timer — a frozen can is a messy can.
  3. Stack smart: Cans chill faster lying on their sides with air flowing around them, so do not pack them tight against the freezer wall.
  4. Chill by the carton: Our 24-can cartons fit a standard fridge shelf when you slide the cans out sideways. Rotate the warm ones to the back.
  5. Cooler on the go: For picnics, freeze a few spare cans the night before. They double as ice packs and are ready to drink once they thaw.

Quick facts:

  • Never leave a regular can in the freezer overnight — the contents expand as they freeze.
  • Most fizzy drinks taste best between 3 °C and 6 °C.
  • Keep unopened cartons somewhere cool and shaded before chilling.

Stock up on a carton of your favourite and you will never wait for a cold drink again.

title: Coke, Pepsi or Mojo? The Great Bangladeshi Cola Debate
excerpt: Everyone has a side. We break down what makes each cola different — and how to settle it at your next adda.
body:
Ask ten friends which cola is best and you will get eleven answers. In Bangladesh the debate is serious: the global giants share the shelf with a home-grown favourite that people are fiercely loyal to.

The contenders:

  1. Coca-Cola: Spiced, vanilla-forward and a little sharper on the fizz. Often described as the "classic" cola taste.
  2. Pepsi: A touch sweeter with a citrus-leaning bite. Many people find it easier to drink quickly.
  3. Mojo: The local favourite. Affordable, boldly flavoured and available in 250 ml, 330 ml and zero-sugar versions.
  4. The imported 330 ml cans: Same brands, a different bottling — worth trying side by side.

Settle it with a blind test:

  • Chill three cans to the same temperature.
  • Pour into identical glasses and have a friend label them secretly.
  • Score for sweetness, fizz and aftertaste — then reveal.

Our 6-packs make the perfect blind-test kit. Pick one of each and let the taste buds decide.

title: Top 5 Cans for a Perfect Iftar Table
excerpt: Break your fast in style. Our five favourite cold cans to pair with piyaju, beguni and haleem.
body:
After a long day of fasting, nothing hits like a cold drink next to the iftar spread. Here are the cans our community reaches for most.

Our iftar line-up:

  1. Clemon Lemon Soda: Tangy and light — brilliant with fried snacks.
  2. Sprite: Crisp lemon-lime that cuts through rich, spicy dishes.
  3. Mojo Cola: A bold, affordable cola for big family tables.
  4. Fanta Orange: A sweet, fruity favourite for the kids.
  5. Rani Float Mango: Dessert in a can, with real fruit pieces.

Iftar tips:

  • Order a carton ahead of time so your cans are chilled before sunset.
  • Serve over ice with a lemon wedge for an easy upgrade.
  • Mix and match flavours with a 6-pack of each.

Plan your table early — cartons sell out fast in the weeks before Ramadan.

title: Zero Sugar Cans: Are They Worth Trying?
excerpt: Coke Zero, Pepsi Black, Mojo Zero and more — what zero-sugar actually means and how they taste.
body:
Zero-sugar cans have become some of our most-ordered products. If you have never tried one, here is what to expect.

What does zero sugar mean?

These drinks use low- or no-calorie sweeteners instead of sugar, so the can contains no added sugar. The taste is designed to be as close as possible to the regular version.

Zero-sugar cans we stock:

  1. Coke Zero Sugar: The closest match to classic Coca-Cola.
  2. Pepsi Black: Bold, with a slightly sharper finish.
  3. Mojo Zero: The local favourite, sugar-free.
  4. Monster Ultra and Red Bull Sugarfree: Energy drinks for those who skip sugar.

Good to know:

  • Taste is personal — try a single can before buying a carton.
  • Check the can label for ingredients and caffeine content.
  • If you have a health condition, ask your doctor what suits you.

Curious? A 6-pack is the easiest way to find your favourite.

title: How to Host the Perfect Adda with a Carton of Cans
excerpt: Birthday, office hangout or rooftop adda — a simple plan for serving everyone without the stress.
body:
A good adda needs three things: great company, good snacks and cold drinks that never run out. The last one is the easiest to get right.

Your party plan:

  1. Count the cans: Plan on two to three cans per guest for an evening. A 24-can carton covers eight to ten people.
  2. Mix the flavours: Include a cola, a lemon-lime, an orange and one zero-sugar option so everyone is happy.
  3. Chill ahead: Put cartons in the fridge the day before, or use a bucket of ice and salt for last-minute cooling.
  4. Set up a drinks corner: A tub of ice, a bottle opener for glass bottles and a bin for empty cans keeps things tidy.
  5. Order early: Choose cartons at checkout and add a note with your event date.

Bonus ideas:

  • Float a few lime slices in the ice tub.
  • Offer fuchka, chotpoti or kebab rolls to match the fizz.
  • Recycle cans — aluminium is endlessly recyclable.

Order a carton or two and spend the party with your friends, not at the shop.
